entry.title: Unveiling the Basin-Like Loss Landscape in Large Language Models
entry.summary: We study the loss landscape of large language models and discover expansive capability basins in parameter space. We introduce a Gaussian-augmented optimizer that enlarges the basin while preserving plasticity. Experiments across model scales demonstrate reduced catastrophic forgetting after adversarial fine-tuning, and we prove a bound connecting basin size to robustness.

entry.title: Compute-Efficient Adversarial Training for Large Language Models
entry.summary: Adversarial training improves language model robustness but is computationally expensive. We propose a sample-efficient inner maximization method for robust fine-tuning of LLMs. Experiments on three jailbreak benchmarks achieve stronger robustness with 42% less compute than standard adversarial training. Code is available at https://github.com/example/efficient-at.

entry.title: Post-Training Data Selection for Reasoning Language Models
entry.summary: We investigate data selection for post-training large language models. Our method combines influence estimates, data quality filtering, and curriculum sampling to select instruction data. Experiments demonstrate improved reasoning performance over random selection and data mixture baselines using half of the training examples.

entry.title: On-Policy Distillation with Adaptive Token Reweighting
entry.summary: On-policy distillation reduces the distribution mismatch between training and inference for large language models. We introduce adaptive token-level teacher feedback over student-generated trajectories. Extensive experiments on mathematical reasoning benchmarks outperform off-policy knowledge distillation while reducing teacher queries.

entry.title: A New Benchmark for Autonomous Driving with Vision-Language Models
entry.summary: We introduce a vision-language model benchmark for autonomous driving and medical image segmentation. The dataset contains images from urban environments and evaluates object detection and visual question answering.

entry.title: Sharpness-Aware Data Selection for General Neural Networks
entry.summary: We connect loss landscape sharpness to data selection in general neural networks. The proposed influence score selects examples that flatten the training objective. Experiments on image classification provide an ablation study and demonstrate improved robustness.
